title: Holding a line of sight from a moving platform.
standfirst: Q-Axis Motors was founded in 2021 by three engineers, each with more than 19 years in control systems, optics or data science. From Mysuru, they build the gimbals and pointing systems that keep a camera or a laser on target while the platform carrying it moves.

hero.alt: Robotics test rigs in an ARTPARK lab
hero.caption: Robotics test rigs in an ARTPARK lab. ARTPARK photograph, not of Q-Axis Motors.

lead: A camera on a drone, a sensor on an aircraft, a laser terminal on a satellite: each is useful only while it stays pointed where it should. The platforms carrying them vibrate, turn and drift. Q-Axis Motors builds the hardware that holds the line of sight steady through all of it.

The company describes its work as building India’s own capability in precision stabilisation, targeting, situational awareness and laser communication. ARTPARK’s portfolio calls it “India’s strategic eye in the sky”.

quote.text: Keeping a camera on a target is easy on a tripod. On a moving platform it is a control problem, an optics problem and a data problem at once. That is the work the three of us had spent our careers on.
quote.who: Preetham K Shivanna, Founder and CEO, Q-Axis Motors

blocks: Preetham K Shivanna, founder and CEO, studied at IIT Madras and has spent more than 19 years in systems architecture, robotics and control systems. He holds a patent in position feedback systems, the sensing that tells a gimbal exactly where it is pointing.

Rabi Kisku, co-founder and COO, is also from IIT Madras, with more than 19 years in optical systems, mechanical design and structural analysis. Ramana Reddy, co-founder and Chief AI Officer, studied at BITS Pilani and has more than 19 years in data science and neural networks. The company was registered in Karnataka in 2021.

sections.h2: Steady to a fraction of a degree.
blocks: Q-Axis Motors says its systems stabilise to better than 100 microradians, with very low latency. They are designed for drones, aircraft, satellites, ground stations, autonomous systems and robotics.

panel.title: What Q-Axis Motors builds
items: Gyro-stabilised gimbals and electro-optical and infrared (EO/IR) payloads.
Systems that find a target and stay locked on it.
Electro-optical and communication payloads combined in one unit.

blocks: The company lists a ₹2 crore pre-seed from IISc-ARTPARK, under the Department of Science & Technology, Government of India, and a ₹75 lakh pre-seed from Point One Capital.
